# Ceramic references: volume, thickness and size from holes, outline and mass (generated by ceramic_volume_check.py)

k = 0.80, 27 °C. Hole diameters are the photo rims of the measurement scripts. *Rim − 1 mm* allows for the rounded, unglazed lip. All numbers are rough; read the ranges.

## 1. Spencer (165 mm, 330 g, A4–F6): air volume

Three inputs, each rough: the twelve holes, the mass, and the thickness read on the edge view (photo 09: 35–45 mm; the instrument's own scale gives the low end, the width of the fingers the high end).

### 1a. From the holes (lowest note A4)

Thumb holes 12 ± 2 mm. The chimney is the wall at the hole. The workshop photo of an open half (photo 11) shows about 3 mm at the thumb holes, which sit at the bottom of pockets; the wall at the finger holes is not known.

| Chimney at the holes, mm | V0, cm³: rim − 1 mm, thumbs 10 mm | rim − 1 mm, thumbs 12 | rim, thumbs 12 | rim, thumbs 14 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 3 | 88 | 94 | 112 | 118 |
| 4 | 79 | 85 | 102 | 109 |
| 5 | 73 | 79 | 94 | 101 |
| 6 | 67 | 73 | 88 | 94 |

Range 67–118 cm³. With walls of 5–6 mm (the first pass): 67–101 cm³.

### 1b. From the outline, the thickness and the mass

Outer volume = π/4 × thickness / width × ∫ width² (elliptical sections; a fuller section adds up to 8 %). Fired clay = (330 g − mouthpiece) / density. Air = outer − clay. The two numbers in a cell are for a mouthpiece of 35 g and of 55 g.

| Thickness mm | Thickness / width | Outer cm³ | Air, clay 1.9 g/cm³ | Air, clay 2.1 | Air, clay 2.3 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 35 | 0.61 | 151 | -4–6 | 11–20 | 23–31 |
| 38 | 0.67 | 164 | 9–19 | 24–33 | 36–44 |
| 42 | 0.74 | 181 | 26–37 | 41–50 | 53–62 |
| 45 | 0.79 | 194 | 39–49 | 54–63 | 66–75 |
| 48 | 0.84 | 207 | 52–62 | 67–76 | 79–88 |
| 51 | 0.89 | 220 | 65–75 | 80–89 | 92–101 |

### 1c. Where the routes meet

- The mass route reaches the holes route (67–118 cm³) only from a thickness of **43.5 mm** up. At 45 mm, the top of what the edge view allows, the two overlap at **67–75 cm³**.
- A thickness of 35–40 mm with 330 g would leave at most 31 cm³ (35 mm) to 53 cm³ (40 mm) of air: too little for A4 with these holes. So the body is at the thick end of the edge-view reading, or lighter than 330 g.
- **Working value: about 70 cm³ of air (65–80), in a body about 45 mm thick (thickness / width 0.79).** The fired clay is then 124–150 cm³: about two thirds of the body is clay. The three inputs only just meet, so this value needs a dense clay (2.1–2.3 g/cm³) and the thick end of the photo reading.
- The first pass read thickness / width 0.8–0.9 (44–56 mm) from the holes and the mass alone. The edge view cuts the top of that range.
